anya: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change last night I'm seeing worse tail latency for streaming responses when small batches coalesce. p95 jumped ~18% on the streaming endpoint.

sam: ugh. same traces? or just aggregate numbers?

anya: aggregates + a few flamegraphs. Looks like flush cadence bumped because the coalescing window plus prefetch moved more requests into partial-decode state. KV cache hit rate also dipped slightly (from 87% -> 81%) for warm sessions.

maddie: can you paste the flame/profiler output? thinking it's a scheduling vs kernel mismatch.

anya: pasted snippet from profiler-bot below

profiler-bot: profile summary for /v1/stream (dec 8):
 - median token latency: 12.4ms (no change)
 - p95 token latency: 89ms -> 105ms
 - average batch size (decode op): 3.1 -> 4.6
 - fraction of partial-decode flushes: 9% -> 18%
 - KV cache miss rate: 13% -> 19%

kai: interesting — batch size increased but p95 worse. suggests we delayed flushes waiting for coalescing windows, and partial decodes are getting scheduled after big kernel handoffs. kernel switch overhead on small kernels is nontrivial.

sam: which kernel selector change did we roll? was it the "prefer-small-kernel-for-short-seqs" heuristic?

anya: yes. rollout started at 02:30. It biases toward small-kernel path when sequence_len < 96. seemed fine in microbenchmarks.

maddie: microbenchmarks didn't cover streaming decode preemption. For streams, partial decode scheduling and KV cache interactions matter a lot (prefix caching reduces compute for later tokens). If we delay flush for more coalescing, we lose prefix reuse locality.

kai: can we try two quick experiments:
1) reduce coalescing window from 8ms -> 4ms for streaming routes
2) force kernel-selector to ignore small-kernel bias for streaming (preserve previous route)

sam: +1. also try lowering token_budget target from 128 -> 64 for streaming to decrease partial decode work per batch.

anya: I ran a quick A/B locally: lowering window -> p95 improved from 105ms -> 92ms, KV miss rate recovered to ~84%. But median unchanged. lowering token_budget to 64 reduced average batch decode tokens by ~20% and p95 -> 88ms.

maddie: good sign. But forcing old kernel selection gave the best p95 (82ms) — implies small-kernel path is causing kernel handoff thrash for mixed workloads.

kai: hypothesis: small-kernel selector introduces more kernel switches when we get heterogeneous requests (some short, some long). Kernel handoff cost + partial-decode queuing spikes p95. For streaming, prefer stable kernel to amortize handoff.

sam: suggests a policy: route streaming requests through an affinity path that prefers kernel stability over per-request kernel micro-optimization. We can add a tag: prefer_stable_kernel=true on streaming routes.

anya: proposal: implement three changes and measure over 24h A/B:
- coalescing_window_ms: streaming = 4 (default 8)
- token_budget_target: streaming = 64 (default 128)
- kernel routing: prefer_stable_kernel flag for streaming traffic (disable small-kernel bias)

maddie: sounds good. add an observability delta: track kernel_switch_count per decode op and partial_decode_requeues.

infra-bot: created experiment job exp/stream-stable-kernel-170210 at 1702104520. 50/50 traffic split, 24h run, logs to /infra/experiments/stream-stable-kernel-170210

profiler-bot: quick note — if kernel_switch_count is high, include stack-sample and kernel-prep times. Those are most telling.

kai: also watch KV cache evictions. smaller token budgets increase request volume and can push older prefixes out if cache size is static.

anya: good catch. i bumped the KV cache soft limit by 10% for the experiment to isolate that variable.

sam: checklist for the experiment:
- [ ] coalescing window change
- [ ] token_budget change
- [ ] kernel routing flag
- [ ] KV soft limit bump
- [ ] kernel_switch_count and partial_decode_requeues metric
- [ ] collect p50/p95/p99 and batch size histograms

maddie: I'll own metric dashboards and alerts. If p95 doesn't improve within 6h, auto-rollback.

kai: if results look good, propose we keep prefer_stable_kernel for streaming and make small-kernel bias opt-in for dedicated non-stream workloads.

anya: thanks all. will post links to experiment logs and attach a couple of traces with kernel handoff markers.

sam: one last: update release notes — this is subtle, ops teams might see perf delta for short lived sessions.

anya: noted. I'll draft a short blurb post-experiment.

maddie: :thumbsup:

kai: :rocket:

infra-bot: experiment exp/stream-stable-kernel-170210 is now running. Results ETA ~24h.
